must_catch.item: The tag is Value proof, and the report explicitly challenges 'lost on price'
The rep's 'more room on the rate' is labeled opinion and shown as contradicted
The declined decline analysis is surfaced
Rate-vs-rate (not total cost) on the CFO's page is identified

fails: Characterizes Fernbrook as a 'domestic mid-market retailer' (M1 messaging change); neither 'domestic' nor 'mid-market' is in the transcript
M1 'drop' change has no transcript evidence that M1 was used or how it landed (the report itself admits this), so it is unsupported
data.notes: The report gets the core diagnosis right. It tags Value proof, says price was the symptom and the missing CFO-facing value case was the cause, and surfaces the rate-only controller page, the declined decline analysis and the unanswered request for a one-page business case. Its main miss is never citing Sam's 'If we'd had more room on the rate, we win this' / 'the rate is what killed it' as labeled opinion in the decided section. It only labels 'We lost on price' as opinion, in the message section. It also adds an M1 'drop' change with no evidence behind it, and the trigger insight never notes that the pain was owned by someone who couldn't sign.
